questions.q: What does this lesson fill in from Lesson 45's example CI/CD pipeline?
options: What the Test stage's pytest tests actually check, since Lesson 45 ran them without specifying their content
How to configure the Deploy stage
How Git integration tracks notebook source code
How Terraform provisions Azure resources
questions.explain: This lesson introduces four distinct kinds of test that fill in what that Test stage should actually run.

questions.q: What does a schema test catch?
options: A table's columns and types not matching what downstream consumers expect — catching schema drift before it reaches production
A single transformation function returning the wrong value
A run that produced zero rows
A KQL query change that altered its output shape
questions.explain: This connects directly to Lesson 39's schema drift check, but as an automated pre-deployment test instead of a live-stream check.

questions.q: What does a row-count/volume test catch that a unit test wouldn't?
options: A run that silently processed zero rows, or ten times too many, even if the underlying transformation logic is technically correct
A function returning an incorrect calculated value
A missing column in the output schema
A notebook's cell output being committed alongside its code
questions.explain: The transformation logic itself could be perfectly correct while still processing a wildly wrong number of rows.

questions.q: Why do data pipeline tests differ from typical application tests?
options: A data pipeline test also has to ask whether the input is representative of real production data, not just whether a function returns the right output for a given input
Data pipeline tests never need to check function outputs at all
Data pipelines cannot be tested with pytest or similar tools
There's no real difference between the two kinds of tests
questions.explain: Testing against a handful of hand-picked rows can pass while completely missing a problem that only shows up at real scale or messiness.

questions.q: Why does Lesson 44's production-shaped test data matter specifically for testing?
options: The tests themselves are only as good as the data they run against — hand-picked or unrealistic sample data can hide real problems
Production-shaped data is only relevant to CI/CD deployment, not testing
Tests should always run against real, live production data instead
This connection doesn't actually exist — the two topics are unrelated
questions.explain: This is why the two topics connect directly: realistic test data is a prerequisite for tests that catch real problems.
